newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end flat in rudderless trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end flat in rudderless trade.

text.p: Share prices at Bombay exchanges ended little changed on Monday, searching for concrete direction in a quiet trading session, traders said.
Foreign fund activity was lacklustre but the broader market showed signs of a strong undertone as select stocks attracted good buying interest, they said.

"It was a dull day. The outlook is still mixed after the political chaos that we saw over the week-end," said Vetri Subramaniam, vice-president, equity sales at institutional brokerage, SSKI Securities.
Laloo Prasad Yadav, who heads a breakaway group of the ruling United Front coalition last week resigned as Bihar chief minister four weeks after being indicted in a $280 million scam.
Analysts said Yadav's immediate move to install his wife, Rabri Devi, as his sucessor was a tragicomedy of democracy.

"What makes the whole thing a farce is that someone with no political experience or mass support can become a chief minister," Yogendra Yadav, a political commentator at the Centre for the Study of Developing Socities, told Reuters.

In stock market action, shares of term-lending bank, Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) ended 3.35 rupees, or 4 percent, higher at 88.25 on the Bombay exchange ahead of its first quarter 1997/98 results.
After market hours, the firm said its first quarter net profit in the three months to June 30, 1997 rose to 2.23 billion rupees from 1.0 billion in the year-ago period.
Shares of diversified firm Wipro Ltd, surged nearly ten percent, at 920.0 rupees ahead of the company's board meeting later this week to consider a bonus share issue.
